author: Jacob A. Riis
title: How the Other Half Lives: Studies Among the Tenements of New York
edition: New York: Charles Scribner’s Sons, 1890. Project Gutenberg ebook 45502 transcription of the Scribner’s text, whose title page (1890) and copyright leaf (“Copyright, 1890, by Charles Scribner’s Sons”; Trow’s Printing and Bookbinding Company) are transcribed; PG records that it was produced from Internet Archive page images; printing otherwise undated. Paragraph boundaries, spelling, punctuation and underscore emphasis markers are retained; prose line wrapping is joined with spaces. Illustration captions that fall between selected paragraphs are omitted. Riis’s photographs are not reproduced. The library text runs from Riis's Preface and the Lowell epigraph through the Introduction, Chapters I–XXV and the statistical Appendix; the title page, contents, list of illustrations, every illustration caption and the transcriber's note are omitted. Riis's footnotes keep the transcription's bracketed form (“[Footnote 4: …]”) as their own blocks where the file places them, with their numbered callouts; tables keep the transcription's line layout as preformatted blocks. The transcription keeps the callout of Chapter VI’s note on “155 deaths of children” but not the note; it is restored from the 1890 page (Internet Archive howotherhalflive00riis_1, p. 61) as “[Footnote 8: …]” after its paragraph (block 85), and the nightly ranges after it moved down one block. Notes 4 and 17 belong to the captions of the plan “Tenement of 1863, for twelve families on each flat” (Chapter I) and the picture “In Poverty Gap, West Twenty-eighth St. An English coal-heaver’s home” (Chapter XIV); with the captions omitted they keep their places (blocks 25 and 230) without a callout. The passages read by the Grade 11 calendar readings (blocks 14–17, 22–28, 30–31, 36–48, 50–65 and 69–70) were also compared word by word with that copy’s OCR text and, where they differed, its page images; no readings changed. The passages of Chapters V–VIII read by the Grade 11 calendar readings (blocks 72–77, 79–102, 104–117 and 119–133) were compared the same way, punctuation and quotation marks included; one reading changed: “the doctor's thermometer” (block 97, where the transcription had “the doctors thermometer”). The passages of Chapters IX and X read by the Grade 11 calendar readings (blocks 135–147 and 149–165) were compared the same way, case, punctuation and quotation marks included; three readings changed: “anything, however wrong” (block 135, where the transcription had no comma), “there is recovery; for” (147, “recovery:”) and the printing’s misprint “more that seventy per cent.” (152, where the transcription had corrected it to “than”), which stands as printed.

rights.basis: The transcribed title page and copyright leaf identify the 1890 Charles Scribner’s Sons text; published before 1931, its US copyright term has expired as of 2026. Project Gutenberg identifies ebook 45502 as public domain in the USA.
